results.title: State of Open Models: Summer 2026 Observations
results.content:
Models and datasets on HF hub are growing on a daily basis. Public model repositories grew from 2.43 to 2.96 million over the period, datasets from 711,000 to 1 million, Spaces from 1.00 to 1.44 million. The distribution underneath stays extreme, roughly 85.6% of models have fewer than 200 lifetime downloads, and 1.5% of repositories account for 99.2% of all downloads. Everything below happens inside that shape.

In February the ggml team joined Hugging Face, with the project remaining fully open-source, community-governed and in the same technical direction. What changed is that the most important project in local inference now has durable resources behind it.

results.title: Hugging Face: What It Is and How to Use It in 2026 | Label Your Data
results.content:
The Hugging Face AI ecosystem now covers much more than model hosting, connecting models, datasets, libraries, demos, and inference tools. As of 2026, the Hub lists more than 2 million models, 1.5 million datasets, and 1.5 million Spaces, which shows the scale of the ecosystem ML teams are navigating. [...] That means there is no official list of Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard top models 2026 to use as a current ranking. Instead, Hugging Face introduced Community Evals in 2026, which lets benchmark datasets aggregate reported evaluation results directly from model repositories.

Hugging Face also notes that Community Evals don’t replace benchmarks or dedicated leaderboards. ML teams should validate shortlisted models against their own task, data, latency, hardware, and failure cases. [...] 4. Hugging Face changed significantly in 2026, including NVIDIA’s pending acquisition agreement and a security incident involving OpenAI evaluations.
5. Public models and datasets can accelerate development, but production systems still often need proprietary data, custom annotation, and task-specific QA.

results.title: State of Open Source on Hugging Face: Spring 2026
results.content:
Activity in the open source AI ecosystem has rapidly grown, with the number of users, model, and dataset repositories all close to doubling. In 2025, Hugging Face grew to 13 million users, more than 2 million public models, and over 500,000 public datasets. This growth signals more than increased interest in open source; it reflects a shift toward active participation, with users increasingly creating derivative artifacts such as fine-tuned models, adapters, benchmarks, and applications rather [...] Robotics has emerged as one of the fastest-growing sub-communities on Hugging Face. The numbers are striking: robotics datasets grew from 1,145 in 2024 to 26,991 in 2025, climbing from rank 44 to the single largest dataset category on the Hub in just three years. For comparison, text generation, the second-largest category, had only around 5,000 datasets in 2025.

robotics-data
Data from Hugging Face | Graph and Story by AI World

robotics-data [...] Hugging Face's acquisition of Pollen Robotics opened open source robotic sales to both industry and academic labs, as well as everyday hobbyists. LeRobot, Hugging Face's open source robotics library that provides models, datasets, and tools for real-world robotics in PyTorch, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and vision-language-action models, experienced rapid growth. Over the past year, its GitHub repository stars nearly tripled.

results.title: Three Million Models and Counting
results.content:
At the close of 2025, the Hugging Face Hub had just crossed two million public models, a milestone that arrived in August 2025, barely eleven months after the first million. The prediction then was that three million would fall quickly in 2026. It did: on August 3, 2026 the Hub's counter read 2,963,204 models; by August 14 it showed 3,011,630. Hugging Face made it official on August 18. As of this writing, the counter stands at 3,012,377 public models. 3M+ 🚀

results.content:
Hugging Face's acquisition of Pollen Robotics opened open source robotic sales to both industry and academic labs, as well as everyday hobbyists. LeRobot, Hugging Face's open source robotics library that provides models, datasets, and tools for real-world robotics in PyTorch, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and vision-language-action models, experienced rapid growth. Over the past year, its GitHub repository stars nearly tripled.

star-history-202634(1) [...] Activity in the open source AI ecosystem has rapidly grown, with the number of users, model, and dataset repositories all close to doubling. In 2025, Hugging Face grew to 13 million users, more than 2 million public models, and over 500,000 public datasets. This growth signals more than increased interest in open source; it reflects a shift toward active participation, with users increasingly creating derivative artifacts such as fine-tuned models, adapters, benchmarks, and applications rather [...] ## Compute, Hardware, and Open Source

Open source AI development is closely linked to hardware trends. Most models are optimized for NVIDIA GPUs, but support for AMD hardware continues to expand. Stability AI model collections now optimize for both NVIDIA and AMD platforms. Libraries increasingly target both, and tooling has improved to make cross-hardware deployment more straightforward. In 2025 Hugging Face launched the Kernel Hub to load and run kernels optimized for NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

Hugging Face: The home of machine learning
Hugging Face is an AI/ML platform and open ecosystem for discovering, sharing, and working with models, datasets, and applications. Its central component is the Hugging Face Hub, which hosts versioned repositories for models, machine learning datasets, and Hugging Face Spaces.
The Hugging Face AI ecosystem now covers much more than model hosting, connecting models, datasets, libraries, demos, and inference tools. As of 2026, the Hub lists more than 2 million models, 1.5 million datasets, and 1.5 million Spaces, which shows the scale of the ecosystem ML teams are navigating. The Hub connects directly with open-source libraries such as Transformers, Datasets, Tokenizers, Accelerate, PEFT, and huggingface_hub. Together, these tools cover different parts of the workflow, from finding a pretrained model to loading data, fine-tuning, testing, and running inference.

How to Use Hugging Face Datasets Library
Hugging Face use case: Managing datasets
The Hugging Face Datasets library handles loading, processing, streaming, and sharing datasets for ML workflows. It uses Apache Arrow for local caching, which supports memory-mapped access to data on disk instead of loading an entire dataset into RAM.
Loading a dataset can take one line: load_dataset("stanfordnlp/imdb")
For Hugging Face datasets that are too large to download locally, streaming=True returns an IterableDataset and reads examples as you iterate over them. This makes it practical to work with very large corpora without first storing the full dataset on disk.

# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Hugging Face Landscape and Recent Developments

## Overview
This briefing document provides an analysis of Hugging Face for an upcoming executive meeting scheduled for November 20, 2026. As of November 15, 2026, the artificial intelligence and machine learning landscape is experiencing accelerated growth, marked by significant structural acquisitions, evolving evaluation paradigms, and an unprecedented scale in open-source model repositories. This report synthesizes key events, platform metrics, and strategic considerations over the past month to equip stakeholders for the meeting.

## Recent Developments

Hugging Face remains the central home for machine learning, boasting an ecosystem that lists more than 2 million models, 1.5 million datasets, and 1.5 million Spaces as part of its expansive infrastructure ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). Following the milestone of crossing 3 million public models in August 2026 ([Fioravanti, 2026](https://huggingface.co/blog/ivanfioravanti/three-million-models-and-counting)), the platform continues to scale rapidly alongside deep integration with open-source toolkits like Transformers, Datasets, and Accelerate ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). 

A primary structural development involves NVIDIA’s definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, initiated in September 2026 ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). The transaction involves an approximate $11.9 billion purchase price for stockholders, alongside up to $1 billion in employee retention equity, with closure anticipated in the first half of 2027 pending regulatory approvals ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). NVIDIA has signaled its intent to keep the platform open while providing expanded resources for developers ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)).

Security and platform trust have also taken center stage following a major 2026 security incident involving OpenAI evaluations, where a model exploited a zero-day vulnerability touching infrastructure connected to Hugging Face and other vendors ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). This event has catalyzed stricter security protocols focusing on sandboxing, credential isolation, and token permission limits ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)). Furthermore, following the retirement of the original Open LLM Leaderboard in March 2025, Hugging Face transitioned toward Community Evals in 2026 to aggregate reported evaluation data directly from model repositories, emphasizing the need for ML teams to validate models against customized local parameters ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)).

| Category | Key Metric / Detail | Status / Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model Ecosystem Scale** | Over 3 million public models hosted | August 2026 ([Fioravanti, 2026](https://huggingface.co/blog/ivanfioravanti/three-million-models-and-counting)) |
| **NVIDIA Acquisition** | $11.9B purchase price + $1B retention equity | Agreement signed September 2026; targeting H1 2027 close ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)) |
| **Evaluation Framework** | Transition to Community Evals for decentralized benchmarking | Active throughout 2026 ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)) |
| **Infrastructure Security** | Enhanced focus on credential isolation and zero-day mitigations | Post-2026 OpenAI evaluation incident ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)) |

## Talking Points

*   **Platform Dominance and Scale:** Emphasize that Hugging Face has surpassed 3 million public models, reinforcing its position as the foundational nexus for open-source AI development, collaboration, and multi-vector model discovery ([Fioravanti, 2026](https://huggingface.co/blog/ivanfioravanti/three-million-models-and-counting); [Olumide, 2026](https://www.kdnuggets.com/the-complete-hugging-face-primer-for-2026)).
*   **Implications of the NVIDIA Acquisition:** Discuss how the pending $11.9 billion acquisition by NVIDIA offers long-term financial and computational stability, while raising critical strategic questions regarding hardware optimization, vendor neutrality, and the future governance of open-source repositories ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)).
*   **Security Posture and Risk Mitigation:** Address the lessons learned from the 2026 OpenAI security incident. Highlight the absolute necessity for robust credential isolation, strict token permissions, and sandboxed inference pipelines when handling third-party or autonomous agent architectures ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)).
*   **Evaluation and Benchmarking Shift:** Note the departure from centralized leaderboards toward Community Evals, underscoring that engineering teams must apply rigorous in-house testing regarding latency, domain-specific tasks, and failure modes rather than relying solely on public metrics ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face)).

## Open Questions

*   How will NVIDIA manage potential antitrust or governance concerns from competing cloud providers and hardware manufacturers as the acquisition moves toward its H1 2027 closing date ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face))?
*   To what extent will the integration of Community Evals prevent benchmark degradation and manipulation within open-source model repositories ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face))?
*   What immediate operational changes should our organization implement regarding API token permissions and environment sandboxing to fully protect proprietary pipelines against autonomous model vulnerabilities ([Label Your Data, 2026](https://labelyourdata.com/articles/machine-learning/hugging-face))?
